answer: Each identity locks 70 credits and anchors one ferrous buoy at a tundra jetty berth, logging its hull serial and drift fixes. A public current table gives the drift radius for each berth, and a jetty auditor recomputes each track: a buoy outside its radius, missing fixes, or sharing a serial with another key burns the bond. The first buoy costs 30 credits; the kth costs 30+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6024 and 1000 fakes cost 3,027,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-buoy ring fails: one serial cannot sit at two berths at once. An honest operator pays 30 once and recovers the bond after audit.
